_comment: Methodology for expanding into new content verticals without cannibalizing yourself. The biggest risk when scaling content isn't writing bad content — it's writing good content that competes with your own existing good content.

preBuildAudit.description: Before building any new vertical, audit what you already cover. We evaluated 6 verticals and found 2 were already saturated — building into them would have created cannibalization, not growth.
steps: List every entity/topic the new vertical would cover
Grep your entire content directory for each entity name
Check GSC for existing impressions on those entity queries
If >50% of entities are already covered, this is a hygiene fix (update existing pages), not a new vertical build
If <50% are covered, proceed with the new vertical — but exclude the already-covered entities
preBuildAudit.rule: Always grep-verify before building from a research pass. Research agents suggest topics they think are gaps — but they can't see your content directory.

pacedDeployment.description: Ship new content in small batches, then wait for GSC confirmation before the next batch. Dumping 20 pages at once makes it impossible to diagnose what worked.
pacedDeployment.waitPeriod: 7-14 days between batches (GSC needs time to crawl, index, and report)
confirmationSignals: Pages appear in GSC with impressions
No cannibalization clusters forming (check with cannibalization-detector.mjs)
No existing pages lost position on related queries

entityVertical.description: Company profiles, fund profiles, person profiles
entityVertical.strategy: One page per entity. Include structured data (Organization/Person schema). Cross-link to related entities.
entityVertical.saturationCheck: If you already have a page mentioning this entity with >500 impressions, UPDATE that page instead of creating a new one.

dataVertical.strategy: Build the tool/dashboard first, then create 2-3 blog posts that cite the dashboard's data. The dashboard is the pillar; the posts are satellites.
dataVertical.saturationCheck: Check for existing ranking/comparison content on the same category. Two 'best X tools' pages = instant cannibalization.

geographicVertical.strategy: Build a data spine (directory/tracker with real local data), then layer Wire/news content on top. Local backlinks from the businesses you feature close the loop.
geographicVertical.saturationCheck: Check if existing national-level content already ranks for '[city] + [topic]' queries. If so, the national page may need geo-segmentation rather than a new local page.

beforePublishing: Run cannibalization-detector.mjs with the new page's target queries
If any existing page targets the same primary query, do NOT publish — update the existing page instead
If overlap is on secondary queries only, proceed but add cross-links between the pages
afterPublishing: If new cannibalization clusters formed, consolidate immediately — don't wait

queryTypeInsight.description: Entity-anchored questions massively outperform generic definitions. This determines what to write.

example.works: 'How does [Company] make money' — position 2-4, high CTR
example.doesNotWork: 'What is venture capital' — position 65-85, generic query with massive competition

queryTypeInsight.rule: Target '[Entity] + [specific question]' queries, not '[generic term] + definition' queries. The entity gives you natural authority; the generic term puts you against Wikipedia.
